name: IconDisc
need: An icon in a filled disc, at a proportion nobody has to choose. The system already has this shape twice — <BrandMark> caps the brand mark in a rail-item disc, and the site's overview tiles now cap a section icon the same way — and the second time is the promotion trigger. The owner's words when the first attempt came out cramped: make it a rule so it does not happen again. A rule would police the number; a component removes the choice, which is the only thing that makes it unrepeatable.

consideredAlternatives.ref: a lint rule on the ratio
consideredAlternatives.whyNot: It can only fire after someone has written the CSS, and it would have to guess which round element is a disc holding an icon. The mistake is choosing a number at all.
A token cannot hold a relationship between two elements: the disc is one box, the glyph is another, and a token in either place still lets the pair be wrong.
It is the brand's cap specifically: it carries the collapse arrow and its cross-fade, and it is sized to a rail item. Generalising it would mean a brand component that is sometimes not the brand.
A disc for a PERSON or a team, with an initial fallback and a presence dot. An icon is neither, and reaching for it would make every section mark announce itself as somebody.

proposedApi: icon (IconName), size (sm | md — the disc), tone (neutral | primary — the fill), className. The glyph size is NOT a prop: that is the whole point.
sources: Measured 2026-08-25: a 20px glyph in a 32px disc fills two thirds of it and reads as cramped; the brand mark in the rail sits at about half, which is the proportion this system already chose. 48/20 is what the overview tiles landed on by eye after the owner said so.
decision: Approved and built 2026-08-26. Built with TWO steps, not three: the ladder is 32/16 and 48/24, a glyph at exactly half its disc on both, which is the proportion the brand mark in the rail already uses (40/20). There is no `lg` because the third disc the grid offers is 64, half of it is 32, and the icon scale runs 16 / 20 / 24 / 40 — adding a step to a type scale to serve one component is how a scale rots, and rounding to 24 or 40 would put a second proportion on the ladder, which is the one thing this part exists to prevent. The overview tile moved onto it and gave back its four declarations; its glyph grew from 20 to 24 in the same 48 disc, which the screen check would NOT have caught on its own (0.33% of pixels, under the 0.5% tolerance) and which was accepted by looking at the pair.
decidedBy: owner (2026-08-26, told the pending requests to be worked)
